rv.q: This is a potent story, told with imagination and flair.
The bigger problem, though, is that the pacing is so sluggish, and the characters remain flat and two-dimensional.
The three actors create wholly believable and, perhaps more surprisingly, very 21st century characters.
But if you’re going to make a short story a two-and-a-half-hour play, it’s going to need more subtext, less exposition.

cn.t: Mixed reviews greet this Australian Yiddish Theatre adaptation of Singer's classic. Critics praise its theatrical authenticity and modern resonance, but some find it overextended. A bold departure from Streisand's film, with uneven results.
